# An actual five-dimensional projected count density below Grunbaum

For a convex body C in R_z times R_x^d, projecting its mixed measure
onto x gives rho(x)=sum_(k in Z)1_(C_k)(x). If the real base section
is [l(x),u(x)], this is max(0,floor(u(x))-ceil(l(x))+1), not its
continuous width.

The actual d=5 family below has arbitrarily many positive integer
fibers and no half-mass fiber. Its ordinary projected maximal depth
is strictly less than Gamma_5=(5/6)^5. This does not refute the weaker
Gamma_5/2 bound: the displayed common core certifies that bound here.

## 1. Actual many-slice roof and its exact counting density

Let T={x_i>=0, sum_(i=1)^5 x_i<=1}, V=|T|=1/120. Fix an integer
N>=3 and 0<epsilon<=1/7. Define the full convex body

    C={0<=z<=N, x_i>=0, sum x_i<=1,
          sum x_i+(1-epsilon)z<=N(1-epsilon)+epsilon}.   (1)

Its radius profile is the concave piecewise-affine function

    r(z)=1,                             0<=z<=N-1;
         epsilon+(1-epsilon)(N-z),       N-1<=z<=N.

Consequently the actual integer fibers are exactly

    T,T,...,T,epsilon T,                                 (2)

with N copies of T followed by epsilon T. Their convex hull is (1),
so no larger actual middle fibers or unlisted integer slices are being
discarded. Every fiber has positive five-dimensional volume. No one
fiber carries half the mass, since the total mass is (N+epsilon^5)V.

For S=sum x_i in [0,1], the real base section is [0,u(x)], where

    u(x)=min(N,N-(S-epsilon)/(1-epsilon)).

Thus it contains N+1 integers when S<=epsilon and N integers when
epsilon<S<=1. Outside T it is empty. The exact projected density is

    rho=N 1_T+1_(epsilon T),
    integral rho=(N+e)V,  e=epsilon^5.                   (3)

Boundary values have no effect on the ordinary five-dimensional
measure; (3) also gives the canonical closed-slice count on T.

## 2. A rational concurrent cap cover below Gamma_5

Write c=5/6, Gamma=c^5, theta=e/(10N), and use the barycentric
coordinates lambda_0=1-sum x_i, lambda_i=x_i for 1<=i<=5.
Choose the six halfspaces

    H_i={lambda_i>=a_i},
    a_0=1/6+5theta,  a_i=1/6-theta for 1<=i<=5.           (4)

Their thresholds sum to one, as do the barycentric coordinates.
Hence the six caps cover ALL of R^5. Their boundaries pass through
the single point (a_1,...,a_5). They are genuine ordinary halfspaces,
and their cylindrical pullbacks are genuine ambient halfspaces for C.

The tiny simplex epsilon T is strictly inside H_0 and disjoint from
H_1,...,H_5. Indeed theta<=1/150, so a_i>=4/25>epsilon for i>=1,
whereas a_0<=1/5<1-epsilon. Every cut is proper on the large T.
The exact cap masses, divided by V, are

    B_0=N(c-5theta)^5+e,
    B_i=N(c+theta)^5,  1<=i<=5.                         (5)

These follow from the elementary simplex cap fraction
|T intersect {lambda_i>=a}|/V=(1-a)^5.

Here are exact uniform estimates proving the strict gap. Since
c-5theta>=4/5, the difference-of-powers identity gives

    N[c^5-(c-5theta)^5]
      >=5N(4/5)^4(5theta)=128e/125.

Hence B_0<=N Gamma-3e/125<N Gamma. Similarly c+theta<=6/7 gives

    B_i-N Gamma<=5N(6/7)^4 theta=(648/2401)e.

The coefficient satisfies

    Gamma-648/2401=2464277/18670176>0.                  (6)

Thus B_i>B_0, and the cover proves the all-point ordinary upper bound

    D(rho) <= N(c+theta)^5/(N+e)
       <= Gamma-[2464277/18670176]*e/(N+e) < Gamma.      (7)

Every potential center belongs to some H_i, so no location restriction
or centroid optimization is hidden in (7). For example N=3,
epsilon=1/7 gives theta=1/504210 and the exact rational upper bound

    3(5/6+1/504210)^5/(3+1/16807) < (5/6)^5.

The ordinary projected maximal depth has not been identified exactly;
the finite upper cover is sufficient to disprove the proposed Gamma_5
lower bound. The retained N-fold uniform T gives the lower bound

    D(rho)>=N Gamma/(N+e)>Gamma/2                       (8)

at the centroid of T. Therefore this family does not obstruct the
weaker Gamma_5/2 target.

The meeting point in (4) lies in T but outside epsilon T. In particular
this example does not satisfy the additional hypothesis that this
specific constant meeting section lies inside every source fiber.
It refutes an unrestricted ordinary-Gamma theorem for the projected
count density. It makes no claim about that narrower section hypothesis.

## 3. The sampled density is not log-concave

The only positive superlevel shapes of rho are the nested simplices
T and epsilon T, but this does not make rho log-concave. Let
g=(1/6,...,1/6), x=epsilon g and y=(3epsilon/2)g. Then

    sum x_i=5epsilon/6<epsilon,
    sum y_i=5epsilon/4>epsilon,
    sum ((x+y)/2)_i=25epsilon/24>epsilon.

All three points lie in the interior of T, with strict inequalities
relative to the small boundary. Thus rho(x)=N+1 while rho(y) and
rho((x+y)/2) both equal N. The midpoint log-concavity inequality
fails strictly, and remains false on neighborhoods of these points.
Changing density representatives on null boundaries cannot fix it.

This differs from the archived projective-slope counter in
`candidate 0ce014ed03a74ef8`: here there is no
ray Jacobian k^d. Formula (3) is the direct continuous projection
of the actual integer-slice measure, with integer multiplicities.

## 4. Scope and verification

The concurrent cap cover is an all-point upper certificate. Its meeting
point is outside the tiny endpoint fiber, so the example does not impose
a specified affine interior meeting section through every fiber. No exact
ordinary maximum, mixed-depth failure, or universal Gamma_5/2 conclusion
is asserted.

The distinct arbitrary-mixture counterexample below Gamma_5/2 and its
convex-compatibility exclusion are proved in
`candidate 32c90486ff8c59d7`.
The common exact verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_projected_count_density_and_cluster_obstruction.py`.
